outcome: No progress found on the question of whether there are infinitely many prime triplets (p, p+2, p+6) or (p, p+4, p+6); the conjecture remains fully open with no case settled and no bound moved on the specific triplet forms.
summary: The Wikipedia article on prime triplets (checked live, not the frozen revision, only to see whether the lead had been updated) still states the conjecture that there are infinitely many prime triplets of the forms (p, p+2, p+6) and (p, p+4, p+6) as open, and its most recent cited record dates to October 2020 (a 20,008-digit example), which predates the window and in any case is a record-size finding rather than a step toward infinitude (per §3.1, an existence/infinitude question is not advanced by a larger example). Broader searches for 'prime triplet conjecture proof', for AI involvement (DeepMind's AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve, other lab systems) touching prime constellations, and for related sieve-theory work in 2024-2026 turned up nothing that bears on this specific triplet conjecture. The closest adjacent results are: (1) Green and Sawhney's October 2024 proof that there are infinitely many primes of the form p^2+nq^2 for n ≡ 0,4 (mod 6) — a different problem (a binary-quadratic-form representation question, not the triplet-spacing conjecture) and thus out of scope under §3.1's case-vs-variant rule; (2) a July 2025 arXiv preprint ('Heuristic Bounded Prime Gaps via a Chaotic Multidimensional Sieve and Random Matrix Theory', arXiv:2507.17986) which is explicitly heuristic/conjectural, concerns general bounded prime gaps (not specifically the (p,p+2,p+6)/(p,p+4,p+6) triplet forms), has not been digested by experts, and makes no mention of any AI system in its methodology; (3) continued refinement of the Maynard-Tao/Polymath bounded-gaps machinery (the b ≤ 246 result) applied to prime constellations generally, none of which specifically resolves or narrows the triplet infinitude question, which requires a much stronger result than bounded gaps between some pair of primes. No case of the conjecture was settled, no bound specific to prime triplets moved, and no AI system was reported as involved in any of the adjacent work found.
competing_reading: One could argue that general prime-constellation progress (Maynard-Tao sieve methods, Polymath's b≤246 bound, or heuristic sieve extensions like arXiv:2507.17986) constitutes 'progress' on the broader project of proving infinitude of prime k-tuples, of which the triplet conjecture is a special case with k=3. However, none of this work proves infinitely many bounded-gap constellations of the *specific* required shape (differences of exactly 2-and-6 or 4-and-6), and the Hardy-Littlewood/Maynard-Tao apparatus for general admissible tuples is not sufficient to settle any specific triplet's infinitude without further work — so this remains general machinery rather than a case or bound on this problem, and I classify it as no_change_found rather than progress.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (or heuristic/computational claim later confirmed) that either the bounded-gap methods can be specialized to show infinitely many prime pairs differing by exactly 2 and 6 (or 4 and 6) simultaneously, or any peer-reviewed/expert-digested result narrowing the specific triplet forms, would change this classification. Absent that, only a full proof of the Hardy-Littlewood prime k-tuple conjecture (or the specific triplet case) would resolve it.
